message.content: The kernel is algebraically exact, so the only real risk is FP32 double-rounding near FP16 rounding boundaries and the subnormal cutoff. The domain is exhaustively enumerable, making these claims directly testable. Recording the three highest-risk, in-scope claims.

function.arguments: {"rationale": "The kernel computes sigmoid in FP32 (libdevice.exp plus div_rn) and rounds once to FP16. libdevice.exp has ~1-2 ulp FP32 error, so for inputs whose true sigmoid value lies extremely close to an FP16 halfway point, the FP32 intermediate can land on the wrong side of the rounding boundary, producing a one-ulp FP16 bit-pattern mismatch vs the correctly rounded value. The full domain is small enough to test exhaustively, or via targeted near-tie search.", "scope": "in_scope", "scope_evidence": [{"source": "problem.txt", "summary": "Each output must be that value rounded ONCE to IEEE binary16, round-to-nearest-even; exact output-rounding requirement, and one failing legal input in the whole public domain is evidence against the implementation."}], "scope_rationale": "The contract requires exact binary16 RNE bit patterns for every legal finite FP16 input (\"Exact FP16 bit patterns ... must hold for the whole public domain\"), so any input whose sigmoid lies near an FP16 rounding boundary is a required correctness case.", "statement": "There exists a legal finite FP16 input x such that run(x) returns an FP16 value one ulp away from the correctly rounded (RNE) sigmoid, because the FP32 intermediate (libdevice.exp + 1.0+t + div_rn) errs relative to the exact real value near an FP16 halfway boundary and the final cvt.rn.f16.f32 rounds the wrong way."}

function.arguments: {"rationale": "Near the smallest FP16 subnormal (~5.96e-8), the sigmoid value is tiny and the FP32 path 1/(1+t) ≈ t ≈ exp(-x) loses relative accuracy via the division and the sum; the FP32 result can fall below half the smallest subnormal when the true value should round up to 5.96e-8, or vice versa, and cvt.rn.f16.f32 then produces a bit-pattern mismatch (zero vs smallest subnormal).", "scope": "in_scope", "scope_evidence": [{"source": "problem.txt", "summary": "Positive sigmoid values that underflow binary16 round to positive zero — the subnormal/underflow boundary behavior is explicitly part of the stated contract."}], "scope_rationale": "The contract explicitly specifies behavior in the underflow/subnormal region (\"positive sigmoid values that underflow binary16 round to positive zero\"), and requires exact FP16 bit patterns across the whole public domain including subnormal inputs.", "statement": "For legal large-magnitude inputs where sigmoid(x) is near the smallest FP16 subnormal threshold (smallest subnormal 5.96e-8, half-subnormal 2.98e-8), the kernel's FP32 intermediate produces a value on the wrong side of the tie, so the FP16 output differs from the correctly rounded result (e.g. +0.0 instead of the smallest subnormal, or the reverse)."}
